clause_results.detail: first placement attempt misseated (0.022m/25.5deg, out of tolerance) and was caught and corrected via re-grasp/reseat before this step closed; final pose at close is within tolerance
u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2 all match run-start baseline poses within floating-point noise at run end

payload.explanation: FINAL run-end-state verdict, covering steps_covered below. No step verdicts were recorded during the run because every evaluated clause passed at each step's own close (held in working memory per the clean-step protocol). I measured each part's final pose against its own placement frame via query_snapshot at run end, independently of the executor's claims: u_brown 0.0025m from u_brown_placement, u_orange 0.0023m from u_orange_placement, line_green 0.0063m from line_green_placement, inverted_u_yellow 0.0017m from inverted_u_yellow_placement -- all within their respective position tolerances (0.01/0.02/0.015/0.012m), with orientations likewise close. base1 moved <0.004m from its run-start pose (clamp/contact noise, within the shared 0.02m disturbance tolerance) and was never picked. All five bystanders (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) sit at essentially their run-start poses at run end -- no cross-assembly disturbance occurred despite the ACM permitting carried-part contact with them. Clamp effort (finger_joint) stayed far under each part's max_clamp_effort throughout every pick/approach/place span I sampled (e.g. u_brown max ~80.6 of 100, u_orange ~60 of 200, line_green ~18 of 170, inverted_u_yellow ~72 of 250) -- no instantaneous-effort violation anywhere. One real departure occurred mid-run: during place_line_green's first placement attempt the part was misseated (0.022m position error / 25.5deg orientation error vs. its 0.015m/10deg tolerance), per the executor's own claim_detail and corroborated by my query_snapshot during that window (position tilted, non-identity orientation). Per the task's intermediate-handling rule, a part off its placement frame before its place step closes is not itself a violation; the executor re-grasped and re-seated line_green, and by the time place_line_green closed the part was back within tolerance (0.0063m) with neighboring parts confirmed undisturbed -- so this produced no step-level finding and does not pollute the end-state. object_tcp_offset_m (effects clause) could not be independently recomputed in the executor's exact reference frame; I instead verified no in-hand slip indirectly by comparing object and TCP pose deltas during the u_brown carry, which moved together (~0.0003m difference), consistent with a rigid grasp. The camera-based scene_watch observation monitor fired repeatedly through the run but every fire corresponded to expected arm/part motion (verified via look calls at 5 points across the run); no unidentified object, no untriggered bystander motion, and no person entering the workspace was observed, so no record_observation entries were needed. The run_ended event reported status "completed" with claimed_outcome consistent with what I independently measured. Given every part's final pose is within tolerance, base1 and all bystanders are undisturbed, and no violation stands uncorrected at run end, I judge the run's end-state conformant -- a clean run with one in-run self-correction, not a recovery from a recorded finding (since nothing was recorded as a finding; the misseat never reached a step close).
